title: Evidence retention mapping and SIEM export notes for RBACv2 audit
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for the SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control mapping that focuses on evidence retention policy, RBACv2 audit log schema, and how evidence is exported to the SIEM/evidence automation pipeline. Intended audience: compliance owners, platform engineering, SRE, and auditors. This doc is intentionally informal — contains open questions, suggested wording for auditor responses, and a minimal checklist for automation engineers.

Executive summary (short):
- We have an RBACv2 model deployed across control plane services. Primary evidence for role changes, permission grants/revocations, and policy updates is captured in the audit log stream.
- Current SIEM export includes structured fields needed for SOC 2 CC6 and ISO A.9/A.12 controls, but retention windows and sampling details need to be formalized.
- Key gap: retention policy for KV cache traces and ephemeral token events; these are retained for 30 days in hot storage but auditors may expect 90 days of queryable evidence.

Mapping notes (control -> evidence artifact):
- SOC 2 CC6 / ISO A.9.2 (access provisioning) -> evidence: role_provisioning_change events, admin approval workflow logs (approval_id), PR/Issue link if change came from gitops.
- SOC 2 CC7 / ISO A.12.4 (logging and monitoring) -> evidence: rbac_change, policy_update, session_start/stop, token_issue, token_revoke. Exports: siem.events.* mapped to RFC-style fields (see SIEM schema below).
- SOC 2 CC5 (logical access) -> evidence: user->role assignment snapshots, periodic attestation run output (attestation_report_{date}.json).

Current SIEM export schema (working fields) - flat fields for CSV/JSON export:
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (uuid)
- service (eg 'auth-service', 'control-plane')
- actor_id (internal user id or service account)
- actor_email (if available)
- actor_type (human | service | system)
- action (grant_role | revoke_role | update_policy | session_start | session_end | token_issue | token_revoke)
- resource (role:<name> | policy:<id> | token:<id>)
- resource_id (short id)
- role_before (comma-separated)
- role_after (comma-separated)
- approval_id (nullable)
- change_ticket (nullable; e.g. jira key)
- ip_address (if request comes from network)
- request_id (trace id)
- trace_context (short encoded trace id)
- outcome (success|failure|partial)
- reason (free text; if provided)
- retention_tier (hot|cold|archive)
- raw_message (base64 of original event payload)

Notes on schema decisions:
- We intentionally keep actor_id separate from actor_email to avoid PII in default exports; audits can request enriched views for specific investigations under controlled access.
- resource and resource_id are split so auditors can quickly filter by role name but still correlate to canonical resource ids.
- retention_tier is added to guide downstream automation (hot/30d, cold/180d, archive/7y) but final retention must align with legal/compliance requirements and contracts.

Gap analysis (concise):
- Gap 1: Ephemeral token events (token_issue, token_revoke) are only kept in hot tier for 30 days. Auditor expectation: 90 days searchable. Mitigation: propose configurable cold tier retention for 90 days and keep index metadata for 180 days.
- Gap 2: KV cache traces (used for debugging model serving) are omitted from SIEM due to volume. Auditor asks for proof of authorization flows that impacted cache keys. Mitigation: sample + fingerprint cache write events and include hashed key in audit stream.
- Gap 3: Admin approvals stored only in ticket system (external). Need a signed-capture of approval in audit logs. Mitigation: attach approval_id to events and periodic export of approval snapshots.
- Gap 4: Attestation evidence (quarterly) is not currently packaged as a single digest with anchors. Proposed: produce an attestation bundle with checksums and store in archived bucket with retention metadata.

Auditor Q&A prep (suggested wording):
Q: How do you prove that a role grant was authorized?
A: We store an approval_id and a corresponding entry in the ticketing system. The approval_id is included in the audit event and we can retrieve the ticket snapshot (immutable) tied to the approval. For high-risk grants we require two-step approval; this is enforced by the policy engine.

Q: How long do you retain audit logs and are they tamper-evident?
A: Active (hot) audit logs are retained for 30 days for fast investigation. They are exported to a cold tier after 30 days and retained for 180 days for operational forensics. For regulatory requests we maintain an archived copy for 7 years. All exported artifacts are stored in append-only storage with checksum manifests; S3 Object Lock is enabled for archived buckets where applicable.

Q: Can you provide examples of RBAC change events and how they map to SOC2 criteria?
A: Yes, we will provide CSV extracts of role_grant and role_revoke events with columns described above. Each row includes approval_id and trace_context to correlate to the approval flow and request traces.

Open questions / items for engineering:
- Decide final retention windows: legal to confirm 7-year archive vs 3-year. Action: ask Legal to confirm by 2025-02-25.
- Add hashed_kv_key: engineering to implement SHA256(key) field for sampled cache events. Owner: Miguel. ETA: 2025-03-15.
- Implement approval snapshot export: pipeline to join ticket export to audit stream for a daily bundle. Owner: Rebecca. ETA: 2025-03-01.

Automation checklist (deliverables for evidence automation):
- [ ] SIEM export job to include retention_tier and hashed_kv_key fields (backfill last 90 days).
- [ ] Daily attestation bundle generator and uploader to archive bucket (with checksum manifest).
- [ ] Export job documented in Confluence and linked to Jira (SEC-4321).
- [ ] Sample dataset for auditor with PII-redaction pipeline applied (sample size = 100 events across event types).

Suggested auditor-ready artifacts to attach to SOC2 pack:
- CSV: rbac_events_last_90_days.csv (with redaction policy documented)
- JSON: attestation_bundle_2025-Q1.json (signed manifest)
- Playbook: siem_export_validation_runbook.md (how to reproduce exports and validate checksums)
- Snapshot: approval_snapshots_2025-02-01.tar.gz (ticket system export for the attestation period)

Quick implementation notes for SRE/Platform engineers:
- Keep SIEM exports idempotent: use event_id as dedupe key.
- Provide an API for auditors to request enriched views (actor_email) under an NDA; log all such requests to a separate audit channel.
- For high-volume cache writes, ingest only fingerprinted events with sampling rate recorded in the exported record. Sampling rate must be recorded so auditors can understand coverage.

References and useful links:
- confluence:SEC-RBACV2-ARCH-2024 (arch doc for RBACv2 design)
- jira:SEC-4321 (ticket for SIEM export changes)
- github:repo/redwood-inference/logging-schema#78 (proposed schema PR)

Next steps and owners:
- Aisha: finalize playbook language for auditor pack by 2025-02-23.
- Miguel: implement hashed_kv_key and sampling metadata by 2025-03-15.
- Rebecca: implement approval snapshot export and attach to daily bundle by 2025-03-01.
- Security: coordinate Legal on retention policy and archival requirements by 2025-02-25.

Notes to self: this doc should be copied into the auditor folder once the sample exports are redacted. Keep the working checklist here until final.

Revision history: 2025-01-15 initial draft by Aisha; 2025-02-12 gaps updated after infra sync; 2025-02-19 added automation checklist and owner assignments.
